title: Batteries, fuel cells & corrosion
examples: What is the difference between a battery and a fuel cell?
Can you explain how galvanisation stops iron from rusting?
Are all chemical reactions that produce electricity redox reactions?

explain.say: Today we look at how we get electricity from chemical reactions.

items: Energy released flows as electrical current

explain.say: A simple battery uses chemical energy to make a flow of electricity.
A hydrogen fuel cell generates electricity by mixing hydrogen and oxygen.

items: Oxygen gas enters the other side

explain.say: Rusting is corrosion, which is the slow decay of metal from reaction.
Galvanisation protects iron by coating it with a layer of zinc.
In real life, cars use fuel cells to run without needing to recharge a battery.

faq.q: What is the main difference between a battery and a fuel cell?
faq.a: A battery stores chemical energy that can only be used a limited time. A fuel cell, however, continuously uses fuel like hydrogen to make electricity as long as you supply it.
asks: Do I need to recharge a fuel cell?
Is a battery a type of fuel cell?

faq.q: Why is galvanisation used on metal structures?
faq.a: Galvanisation coats the iron with zinc, which is more reactive. This means the zinc corrodes first, protecting the iron underneath.
asks: What is the purpose of zinc coating?

faq.q: Is corrosion always a bad thing for metal?
faq.a: While rust is damaging, some corrosion processes are useful. For example, in batteries, controlled oxidation happens to generate power.
asks: What is the chemical name for rust?

faq.q: How does a fuel cell generate electricity?
faq.a: It uses an electrochemical reaction where hydrogen and oxygen react inside the cell. This reaction releases electrons that flow through an external circuit, creating electricity.
asks: What chemicals are needed for a fuel cell?
Is the reaction in a fuel cell exothermic?

faq.q: What is the role of the electrolyte in a cell?
faq.a: The electrolyte is the chemical solution that allows ions to move between the electrodes. This movement of charge is necessary for the chemical reaction to continue.

facts: Batteries store chemical energy and release it through redox reactions.
Fuel cells generate electricity continuously as long as fuel is supplied.
Corrosion is the deterioration of a material, often metal, due to chemical reactions.
Galvanisation involves coating iron with a protective layer of zinc.

quiz.say: A device that produces electricity from a chemical reaction and needs recharging is a:
quiz.why: A battery stores energy and discharges it over time.

wrong.0: A fuel cell requires a continuous supply of fuel.
wrong.1: The electrolyte is the chemical solution, not the device itself.
wrong.2: Corrosion is the process of decay, not a power source.

quiz.say: What process protects iron by coating it with zinc?
quiz.why: Zinc acts as a sacrificial metal, corroding instead of the iron.

wrong.0: Oxidation is the chemical process, not the method of prevention.
wrong.2: Electrolysis uses electricity to cause a reaction, it is not a protective coating.
wrong.3: Neutralisation involves mixing acid and base to form salt and water.

quiz.say: Which system uses hydrogen and oxygen to generate power continuously?
quiz.why: Fuel cells are designed to use fuels continuously, unlike batteries.

wrong.0: Batteries have a fixed amount of stored chemical reactants.
wrong.1: Galvanisation is a protective coating, not a power generator.
wrong.2: Rusting is the unwanted corrosion of iron.
